quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the vehicle you passed.
When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the vehicle you passed.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only pass if you have enough space to return to the driving lane safely. You need enough room between your vehicle and the one you passed. When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, it is safe to move back.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check the traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use only your rearview mirror.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, you must know what traffic is around you. Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic and be ready for any changes when merging.

questions.question: What lane should you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, this means turning from the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red light at an intersection?

options.text: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed.
Slow down and go forward carefully.
Stop completely and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works the same as a stop sign. You must come to a full stop and then proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you never do when changing lanes?

options.text: Change lanes while you are inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Look for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while you are inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Before you change lanes, always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Watch for other drivers who may move into the same lane.

questions.question: What speed should you drive when merging onto a freeway?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted freeway speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, drive at or near the same speed as the traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: When are large trucks most likely to lose speed?

options.text: When driving up long or steep hills.
When driving through long, gradual curves.
When driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more time to speed up than smaller vehicles, so they lose speed going uphill. Give trucks extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for several hours.
When rain has just started.
When it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain has just started.
questions.explanation: Pavement is slipperiest when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater to create a greasy coating.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid dangerous driving situations?

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of your surroundings. Watch the front, sides, and rear of your vehicle at all times. This helps you see problems and make safe changes to your speed and position.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross the centerline to pass from your side of the road when it is safe.

questions.question: You should signal to turn ____ before you start turning.

options.text: 100 feet
50 feet
10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: You and another driver reach a four-way stop at the same time. The other driver is on your left. Who goes first?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right goes first.

questions.question: In fog or mist, do not use high-beam headlights because:

options.text: The light bounces back into your eyes.
Oncoming cars may not see you.
Cars behind you may drive too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light bounces back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high-beam headlights reflect back into your eyes. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: To avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights:

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the center line.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then look back ahead to track where the other car is.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medicines and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe for driving if used as directed.
All medicines prescribed by a doctor are safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines—prescription or over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines often cause drowsiness. Know how your medicine affects you before you drive.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Start to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Honk your horn loudly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn loudly.
questions.explanation: If a child or pedestrian is about to enter the street in front of your car, honk your horn with a sharp, loud blast to warn them.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right, not a privilege.
Privilege, not a right.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it by following the law.

questions.question: You should always drive at a speed that is:

options.text: The same as other cars around you.
The speed limit.
Right for the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right for the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that is safe for the current road and weather conditions. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: You see a yellow traffic light ahead. You have not yet entered the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Slow down and carefully drive through.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means get ready to stop. If you have not entered the intersection, stop. If you are already in the intersection, cross it quickly.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning in wet conditions, you should:

options.text: Drive at the speed you would use in good weather.
Brake hard as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip on wet roads and ride on top of the water. Driving slowly in rain prevents this. Drive slower in wet conditions than you would in good weather.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the accelerator and brakes. Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid. If you have anti-lock brakes, press firmly on the brakes and steer straight.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to road construction.
The road ahead turns sharply at a sharp angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply at a sharp angle.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions just ahead. This sign tells you to slow down and prepare for a sharp turn.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the roadway.
At the right side of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see the road. Do not retaliate by keeping your bright lights on.

questions.question: At an intersection where you cannot see clearly to the side, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an intersection. If you cannot see cross traffic clearly, stop completely. Then move forward slowly until you can see both directions.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this yellow sign?

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow sign means you are near a school. Watch for children and be ready to stop if they are in the crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that these parking spaces are reserved for people with disabilities. Only vehicles with a disability license plate or placard may park here.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when can you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the front bumper of the other vehicle.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This means you have enough space to safely pull in front.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: You are approaching a railroad crossing. Be ready to stop.
You will always stop at the railroad crossing.
Stop and wait for a signal before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are approaching a railroad crossing. Be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you go.

questions.question: When entering the highway on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?

options.text: Enter the right lane immediately and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder of the main road to reach traffic speed.
Speed up and enter the highway only when you see a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up and enter the highway only when you see a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic before entering. Speed up only after you have found a safe space to merge.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, what must you do?

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must stop completely. This applies no matter which direction you are traveling.
